e-5610.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $10$ | $8$ | $6$ | $3$ |

Find the line of the form $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072172/assets/ba4b73a8acd1ede70da8d25a67159c74420ac2fd11d15c830a460071d881ff42.png)
*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.*
e-5610.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 8 \\ 6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
{\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X^T} X )^{-1}$ and $X^T \mathbf{y}$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{104}[\begin{aligned}26 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}27 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6.75 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y = 6.75 - x.$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 10 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

decision.explanation: The observation vector is the column vector of measured y-values in table order: −6, −5, −1, 1, 1. This is option d.

after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Regression Line in Terms of Matrices and Vectors
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-6$ | $-5$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $1$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$

$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=120[6224],XTy=[243], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

decision.explanation: Multiplying the given matrix and vector gives β₀ = (6·24 + 2·3)/20 = 7.5 and β₁ = (2·24 + 4·3)/20 = 3. Thus the best-fit line is y = 7.5 + 3x.

| $y$ | $1$ | $5$ | $8$ | $10$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 8 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation 

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7.5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=7.5+3x.$

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=120[6−2−24],XTy=[7−9], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a

decision.explanation: The coefficients are β₀ = (6·7 + (−2)·(−9))/20 = 3 and β₁ = ((−2)·7 + 4·(−9))/20 = −2.5. Thus the best-fit line is y = 3 − 2.5x.

after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $5$ | $3$ | $2$ | $-3$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector. 

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=3-2.5x.$
